about: Vectors for the x402/exact/algorand pairing of @integraledger/lcp's avm entry point. H is SHA-256("abc") from FIPS 180-2. The values were computed with py-algorand-sdk 2.12.0 and PyNaCl 1.6.2 on Python 3.12.3, with hashlib's sha512_256 as a second path, 2026-09-25; the seeds are not recorded here. Rounds are decimal strings. The SignedTxn rows of V3's refusals are V2's payment entry decoded and re-encoded with algosdk 3.8.0's msgpackRawDecodeAsMap and msgpackRawEncode (which give V2's entry back unchanged) with one member replaced, and algosdk 3.8.0's decodeSignedTransaction refuses each. The rows of V3's refusals whose case ends "a string that is not well-formed UTF-8 (RFC 3629 §4)" are V2's payment entry with one msgpack string written by hand, its length set to its bytes: in place of one of V2's own strings, a map key or a value, or as the key of one member appended, with the value 5, to the entry's map or to its transaction's map, whose count rises by one; RFC 3629 §4's syntax and Python 3.12.3's strict UTF-8 codec refuse each such string. Rows 12 to 16 of V3's refusals are refused as the x402 path reads them: rows 12, 14 and 15 key a member algod does not know, and rows 13 and 16 write a gen whose bytes the x402 facilitator reads as other text. Rows 17 to 39 of V3's refusals are V2's payment entry written by hand in the msgpack specification's formats, with the member each case names written, appended to the payment transaction's map or added to the entry's, whose count rises by one, or the entry followed by one byte. Each is refused by go-algorand v5.0.3's decoder (go-codec v1.1.10 under go-algorand's CodecHandle) or by Transaction.WellFormed's type rules, or is read by algokit-utils 10.0.0-alpha.46's decodeSignedTransaction, the x402 reference facilitator's decoder, as another signed transaction than algod reads, or refused by it or by its transaction id. The x402 reference facilitator's reading is at x402-foundation/x402 e95b0666 (typescript/packages/mechanisms/avm): it decodes each entry's base64 with Node's Buffer.from(entry, "base64"), which takes other spellings of the same bytes than the canonical one, and lcp reads the canonical form only (RFC 4648 §3.5), so row 11 of V3's refusals is refused. The V4 rows give status's answer under the profile read-status at the one mark, final, asked about the act payment unless a row's query says otherwise; positions are confirmed rounds; V4's own about states the lookup, the search for H and the answers it gives while the facts the search rests on are not yet shown. V3.authorities holds V2's transaction under each authority, and build's row 6 the option at amount "0", each with its source.

authorities.about: V2's payment transaction under each authority a payment entry can carry, at paymentIndex 1 beside V2's fee payer entry. Each entry is algosdk 3.8.0's encodeMsgpack of a SignedTransaction over V2's decoded transaction (the clawback's transaction written by makeAssetTransferTxnWithSuggestedParamsFromObject with V2's members, the fee payer as sender and the payer as asset sender). The logic signatures' program is TEAL version 6's pushint 1, 06 81 01; their delegating key is the Ed25519 key of the seed 0x00…01, public key 4cb5abf6ad79fbf5abbccafcc269d85cd2651ed4b885b5869f241aedf0a5ba29, which is not the payer's: lcp verifies no signature. lsig.sig and lsig.lmsig are algosdk's LogicSig.sign without and with a 1-of-2 multisignature of that key and payTo's, lsig.msig is that multisignature with LogicSig.signProgram's signature, and lsig.pqsig is algosdk's EncodedPQSig of the scheme f1 with a key of 1,793 bytes 0x11, the salt addressFromPQKey derives for it and a signature of 1,538 bytes 0x22. go-algorand v5.0.3 counts a logic signature by its program (LogicSig.HasProgram, data/transactions/logicsig.go:58-61) and reads sig, msig, lmsig and pqsig as its delegations (:36-50). The answers are the profile's: rules 4, 8, 10 and 12.

V4.case: status and recover on Indexer fixtures
V4.about: Constructed fixtures, marked so: each is an answer of the Algorand Indexer's API (api/indexer.oas2.json at algorand/indexer 748ac404), written by hand, not recorded from a running Indexer; the records owed are listed in the profile. A transaction is written with its id, confirmed round, tx-type, sender, auth-addr, the one member of its signature that is set, its note ("H" for H's LCP string, else base64), its asset transfer and its inner transactions. lookup is GET /v2/transactions?txid=; header is GET /v2/blocks/{round}?header-only=true, true where the Indexer answers the header; pages are GET /v2/accounts/{account}/transactions in the order asked, each with the parameters the read must ask. The query asks the act payment at the one mark, final, unless the row says otherwise. expect is status's answer as the read gives it: the facts the search rests on are not yet shown by a run (the profile's rule 16), so a search read to its end answers pending, search-incomplete, at the round it reached, where it would answer failed. Every expected answer was derived by hand from read-status.md and x402-exact-algorand-note.md. The other transaction ids are base32 of SHA-512/256 of a label (Python hashlib).

buyer.about: The buyer gate's rows for this file's pairings, in the form of buyer.json's rows. B2 is the plant: the document advertises H, the hash of the ATR in B6's first check, and the link serves the planted ATR, that ATR with one byte changed; the gate declines hash-mismatch and never calls the signer. B6 is the pairing's bound check over the payment this file already holds: check(ATR, presented) gives H, and check(planted ATR, presented) declines signed-not-bound. Where the ATR is abc, H is its SHA-256 (FIPS 180-2 B.1) and the planted ATR is abd. SHA-256 values are GNU coreutils sha256sum, which openssl dgst -sha256 matches. Bytes are hex. A B2 input names the account, the buyer's inputs and the time (now, in seconds) its build needs. noSignedPayment names each pairing of the file that has no B6 row, and why.

build.about: build's answers for the file's option O, payer and parameters, with the genesis id, and the genesis hash where a row names one, replaced by the row's. \ud800 in a genesis id is a lone surrogate, which UTF-8 cannot encode (RFC 3629 §3). Row 1's group id and payment txid were derived by hand from the signed transaction's canonical form (sorted keys, shortest formats, members at their zero value left out), the group id as SHA-512/256 of "TG" and {txlist: [each transaction's id]}, and each id as SHA-512/256 of "TX" and the transaction; the same derivation gives V2's expectGroupId and expectPaymentTxid from the file's own genesis id. Both readers of the x402 path read row 1's gen with its mark, so bound reads the payment build writes. The mainnet genesis hash is go-algorand v5.0.3's (cmd/algokey/keyreg.go:94). Rows 2 and 3 pin the order of build's checks: the genesis id before the genesis hash. Row 4's genesis id is written as a str 16 (the msgpack specification's formats), so V2's payment entry of 374 bytes, its gen testnet-v1.0 a fixstr of 13, becomes 374 - 13 + 3 + 5,781 = 6,145 bytes, whose base64 is 8,196 characters (RFC 4648 §4), past the 8,192 the carrier reads: build refuses it. A genesis id of 5,780 x gives 6,144 bytes and 8,192 characters, which build writes. Row 6 is the file's option at amount "0", which the scheme admits (no floor; the facilitator compares the amount by equality): its group id, payment txid, fee payer's txid and bytes to sign were derived by hand the same way from V2's two transactions, the payment transaction's aamt, at its zero value, left out of its canonical form and its map's count one less (Python's hashlib).
